readerTitle: Before you hire, write down what 'done well' looks like
caseNote: 가상 사례 두 개 (지역 물류창고의 야간 감독자 채용, B2B 소프트웨어 스타트업의 마케팅 책임자 채용) + 가상 적용 (고객 성공 매니저). 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 채용은 사람을 찾는 일 이전에 '이 자리가 1년 뒤 무엇을 이뤄야 하는가'를 정하는 일이다. 결과를 먼저 쓰면 필요한 능력이 저절로 좁혀진다.
misconception: 좋은 사람을 뽑으면 역할은 알아서 정해진다. 경력 연수와 자질 목록을 적으면 직무 정의는 끝난 것이다.

sources.text: Smart, G. & Street, R. (2008). Who: The A Method for Hiring. (역할의 목적·성과·역량을 먼저 적는 'scorecard' 방식)
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: Smart & Street(2008)의 scorecard가 mission, outcomes, competencies로 구성된다는 설명은 게시 전에 원서로 확인하세요. 카드 본문에서는 책 이름을 쓰지 않고 '많은 채용 가이드'로 일반화했습니다.
창고 오출고율(2%→1%), 초과근무, 이탈률 등 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 실제 업계 평균처럼 읽히지 않도록 카드에 illustrative 라벨을 붙였습니다.

cards.title: Before you hire, write down what 'done well' looks like
body: A warehouse posts an ad: *Night shift supervisor. 5+ years experience. Strong leader. Team player.*
A software startup posts one too: *Head of Marketing. Creative, data-driven, self-starter.*
Both ads sound fine. Both hires will go wrong for the same reason, and it happens before a single candidate applies.

image.label: Two job ads full of vague words like 'rockstar' and 'team player'
image.brief: 게시판에 붙은 구인 공고 두 장. 하나는 창고(지게차 아이콘), 하나는 노트북 아이콘. 두 공고 모두 "Strong leader", "Team player", "Self-starter" 같은 흐릿한 단어가 반쯤 지워진 듯 흐리게 보임. 실제 회사 로고 사용 금지.

cards.title: Your night supervisor just quit.
body: You run a regional distribution warehouse. On the night shift, wrong items are going into boxes more often, overtime is climbing, and two pickers left last month. Now the supervisor has quit too.
What do you write first?

options.text: Update the old job description and raise the experience bar to 7 years
options.feedback: Fast and familiar, but it describes the last person, not the problems you need solved. More years doesn't mean they can fix mis-picks.

options.text: List what the new supervisor must have fixed within 12 months, then work back to the skills that requires
options.feedback: It takes an hour longer, but it tells you who to look for and how to judge them later. That's the idea in this lesson.

options.text: Describe the best supervisor you ever had and hire someone like them
options.feedback: A real person is more concrete than adjectives. But they succeeded at a different job, at a different time, with different problems.

cards.title: Two hires, one missing step.
body: The warehouse hired a veteran from a huge distribution center. He was used to well-staffed shifts and a training team. On a thin night crew with no trainer, mis-picks didn't fall.

The startup hired a talented brand marketer. Six months later, the founders called it "not a fit." It turned out one founder wanted trial signups, another wanted big-company leads, and the CEO wanted a brand. They had never said this out loud.
Neither hire was a bad person. Nobody had decided what the job was for.

image.label: Split scene: a warehouse night shift and a startup meeting, both with question marks
image.brief: 화면을 좌우로 나눈 일러스트. 왼쪽은 야간 창고에서 혼자 고민하는 감독자, 오른쪽은 회의실에서 서로 다른 방향을 가리키는 창업자 세 명과 당황한 신규 마케터. 양쪽 머리 위에 같은 물음표. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Defining the role
body: **Defining the role** means writing down what success in the job looks like, in results you could check, before you look at a single candidate.
A typical job ad lists duties and traits: *experienced, organized, a leader*. A role definition lists outcomes: *what will be different in 6 to 12 months because this person showed up*.
Traits describe a person. Outcomes describe a job. You can only judge whether someone fits a job you have actually described.

cards.title: Three short parts, in this order.
body: Many hiring guides suggest the same simple structure:
list: **Mission:** one sentence on why the role exists
**Outcomes:** 3 to 5 results, each with a deadline
**Skills:** only the ones those outcomes truly require
cards.callout: For the warehouse: *cut mis-picks from 2% to 1% in a year, keep the night crew staffed without extra overtime.* That points to someone who trains and schedules well, not someone with the longest résumé.
cards.softwareNote: For the startup, writing outcomes forces the founders' hidden disagreement into the open. "500 qualified trial signups a month by month nine" calls for a very different hire than "build our brand."

cards.title: The same page guides the whole hire.
body: Once outcomes are written, the rest of hiring gets easier. Interview questions ask how candidates have produced similar results. Candidates can see if they want the job. Weak options drop out early.
It also helps after the hire. On day one, the new person knows what they'll be judged on. At six months, you compare results to the page instead of relying on a feeling.

image.label: One page with outcomes, linked by arrows to the ad, interview and 6-month review
image.brief: 가운데에 "Role: 3 outcomes"라고 적힌 한 장짜리 문서. 화살표가 "Job ad", "Interview questions", "Day one", "6-month review" 네 칸으로 뻗어 나가는 인포그래픽. 단순한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: A role definition can be wrong, or too much.
body: Outcomes are guesses about what the business needs. In a young company, needs shift fast. Revisit the page after 90 days rather than treating it as a contract.

Watch for overload too. Ten outcomes describe a person who doesn't exist, so you'll never hire. And don't slip old filters back in. "Must have a degree" or "10 years" belong only if an outcome truly demands them.

cards.title: Now it's a software company.
body: Your B2B software company is losing too many of its largest customers at renewal. You want to hire a customer success manager.
Which role definition would you post?

options.text: 3+ years in software, excellent communicator, CRM experience, customer-obsessed
options.feedback: Reasonable filters, and easy to write. But nothing says what problem they'll solve, so every friendly applicant looks qualified.

options.text: Within 9 months, cut lost renewals among our 40 largest accounts by half, and run a review with each one every quarter
options.feedback: Clear and checkable. It tells you to look for people who have kept big accounts before, and it tells them what success means.

options.text: Cut lost renewals, handle all support tickets, upsell accounts, write help docs, run the user community
options.feedback: Every item matters, but together they describe three jobs. You'll either never hire or hire someone set up to fail.

cards.title: Decide what the job must achieve before you decide who does it.
body: A good hire starts with a page of outcomes, not a list of adjectives. The skills you need follow from the results you want.
**Try it today:** pick a role you plan to fill, or one you already have. Write three results that role must deliver in the next 12 months. If you can't, you're not ready to hire yet.
